input_messages.content: Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would really like to fix this so I can send pictures to my family. Can you help me with that?
My phone number is 555-123-2002, and my name is John Smith. How can I help you further?

I ran the checks you asked for. It shows that my messaging app cannot send MMS messages. Also, my phone's status bar shows no signal and that mobile data is disabled. The battery is at 80%. What should I do next?

The checks show that Airplane Mode is off, but my SIM card is missing or not detected by the phone. Also, mobile data is not enabled, and there is no cellular service or signal. What should I do next? I'm worried about my phone not detecting the SIM card.

I reseated the SIM card as you suggested. Now the SIM card is active and working. The status bar shows a poor 2G signal, but mobile data is still disabled. What should I do next? I'm a bit relieved the SIM card is working again.

I turned mobile data on. The network status now shows mobile data is enabled, the SIM card is active, and there is a poor 2G signal. The phone is connected to the cellular network. What should I try next?
The network mode preference on my phone is set to 2G only. Since MMS requires at least a 3G connection, should I change this setting? If so, please tell me what to do next.

I changed the network mode preference to 4G/5G preferred. Now the signal strength is excellent, and the phone is connected to a 5G network with mobile data enabled. However, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What should I do next? This is a bit frustrating.

The APN settings show the APN name as "internet" and the MMSC URL is set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I understand these are technical settings and usually best left unchanged. What should I do next?
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON on my phone. Should I turn it off to see if that helps with sending MMS messages? What do you recommend?

I turned Wi-Fi Calling off as you suggested. The phone still has an excellent 5G signal and mobile data enabled, but my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? This is quite frustrating.
The messaging app has permission for storage and phone. It seems to have the necessary permissions for MMS. What should I do next? I'm eager to get this fixed.
I granted the SMS permission to the messaging app as you suggested, but it still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed with all these steps.
I restarted my phone as you suggested, but unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.
Data Saver mode is off, and VPN is turned off as well. What should I try next? I'm hoping we can fix this soon.

The speed test failed and showed no connection, even though the status bar shows an excellent 5G signal and mobile data enabled. This seems strange. What should I do next? I'm worried about losing my connection while abroad.
Data Roaming is currently off on my phone, even though my line has roaming enabled on your side. Should I turn Data Roaming on? If so, please tell me how to do that.

I turned Data Roaming on, and now the speed test shows an excellent connection with a very fast download speed. My messaging app can also send MMS messages now. It looks like the problem is fixed! Thank you for your help.
No, thank you very much for your patience and help. I'm glad the MMS issue is resolved now. Have a great day! ###STOP###

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Thanks. No signal means your phone has no cellular service, and MMS needs service and mobile data. Let's find the cause.

Please run these two checks and tell me the results:
1. **check_network_status**: is Airplane Mode on or off, and is mobile data enabled?

Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
The network mode preference on my phone is set to 2G only. Since MMS requires at least a 3G connection, should I change this setting? If so, please tell me what to do next.

Yes, change it. A 2G-only setting is why MMS can't work.

Please run **set_network_mode_preference** with the mode `"4g_5g_preferred"`. Then run **check_network_status** and tell me the signal strength and network type. After that, run **can_send_mms** again and tell me the result.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I changed the network mode preference to 4G/5G preferred. Now the signal strength is excellent, and the phone is connected to a 5G network with mobile data enabled. However, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What should I do next? This is a bit frustrating.

I understand the frustration. You now have a strong 5G connection, so we can move on to the other causes of MMS problems.

Please run **check_apn_settings** and tell me what it shows for the APN name and the MMSC URL. Is the MMSC URL set?

The APN settings show the APN name as "internet" and the MMSC URL is set to "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." I understand these are technical settings and usually best left unchanged. What should I do next?

The MMSC URL is set, so the APN settings look fine. Next we'll check Wi-Fi Calling, which can interfere with MMS.

Please run **check_wifi_calling_status** and tell me whether Wi-Fi Calling is on or off.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON on my phone. Should I turn it off to see if that helps with sending MMS messages? What do you recommend?

Yes, please turn it off. Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS.

Please run **toggle_wifi_calling** to turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF. Then run **can_send_mms** again and tell me the result.

I turned Wi-Fi Calling off as you suggested. The phone still has an excellent 5G signal and mobile data enabled, but my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? This is quite frustrating.

I know this is frustrating. The last thing to check is the messaging app's permissions. MMS needs both storage and SMS access.

Please run **check_app_permissions** for the app "messaging" and tell me which permissions are listed as granted.

The messaging app has storage and phone permissions, but **sms** isn't listed. MMS needs both storage and sms, so that's likely what's missing.

Please run **grant_app_permission** with app_name "messaging" and permission "sms". Then run **can_send_mms** again and tell me the result.

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I granted the SMS permission to the messaging app as you suggested, but it still cannot send MMS messages. What else can we try? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed with all these steps.

I know this is a lot of steps, and you've done them all well. We've fixed several real problems: the SIM, mobile data, the network mode, Wi-Fi Calling and the SMS permission. Some of those changes may not take effect until the phone restarts.

I know this is frustrating, and I appreciate your patience. A few things are still unchecked, and they can affect mobile data and messaging.

Please run these two checks and tell me the results:
1. **check_data_restriction_status**: is Data Saver mode on or off?
2. **check_vpn_status**: is a VPN connected?
Data Saver mode is OFF.
VPN is turned OFF.
Data Saver mode is off, and VPN is turned off as well. What should I try next? I'm hoping we can fix this soon.

Data Saver and VPN are both off, so neither is the cause. Let's confirm that mobile data works at all.

Please run **run_speed_test** and tell me the result. I'm looking for whether it shows a connection and what the download speed is.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

The speed test failed and showed no connection, even though the status bar shows an excellent 5G signal and mobile data enabled. This seems strange. What should I do next? I'm worried about losing my connection while abroad.

Your line (555-123-2002) already has roaming enabled on our side. You mentioned being abroad, so the next thing to check is the Data Roaming setting on your phone.

Please run **check_network_status** and tell me whether Data Roaming is on or off.

Data Roaming is currently off on my phone, even though my line has roaming enabled on your side. Should I turn Data Roaming on? If so, please tell me how to do that.

Yes, please turn it on. Your line is already roaming enabled, so the phone setting is the only thing left.

Please run **toggle_roaming** to turn Data Roaming ON. Then run **run_speed_test** and tell me the result. After that, run **can_send_mms** again and tell me what it shows.

Data Roaming is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed Test Result: 275.00 Mbps (Excellent). Connection is very fast.
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I turned Data Roaming on, and now the speed test shows an excellent connection with a very fast download speed. My messaging app can also send MMS messages now. It looks like the problem is fixed! Thank you for your help.

Your MMS problem is fixed. The speed test is excellent, and your messaging app can send MMS again. You can send pictures to your family now.

Several things were wrong, and these fixes got it working:
- The SIM card wasn't detected, so we reseated it.
- Mobile data was off, so we turned it on.
- The network mode was 2G only, so we changed it to 4G/5G preferred.
- Wi-Fi Calling was on, so we turned it off.
- The messaging app was missing the SMS permission, so we granted it.
- Data Roaming was off on your phone, so we turned it on.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?
No, thank you very much for your patience and help. I'm glad the MMS issue is resolved now. Have a great day! ###STOP###
